questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the 'balance of trade' of a country?
choices: The difference between the value of a country's imports and exports
The total value of a country's imports and exports
The number of countries a country trades with
The types of goods a country imports and exports
questions.solution: The balance of trade refers to the difference between the value of goods and services a country exports and the value it imports. If exports are higher, it is positive; if imports are higher, it is negative. The other options describe different aspects of trade, such as the total value (which is not the definition of balance of trade) or the number and types of goods traded, which are not what the term specifically refers to.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a bilateral trade agreement?
choices: To trade with multiple countries at once
To encourage trade between all nations globally
To trade with a single country or a few countries
To restrict trade to only one country
questions.solution: A bilateral trade agreement is between two countries, allowing them to trade specified commodities. It is not meant for trading with multiple countries or restricting trade to only one. The other options either overgeneralise or misrepresent the scope of bilateral trade.

questions.stem: What is the basic function of the World Trade Organisation?
choices: To promote free trade and reduce trade barriers
To promote military alliances between countries
To provide financial aid to developing countries
To control the population of the world
questions.solution: The World Trade Organisation's basic function is to promote free trade and reduce trade barriers by facilitating international trade agreements and resolving trade disputes. Military alliances are the responsibility of organizations like NATO, not the WTO. Financial aid to developing countries is typically handled by institutions like the World Bank or IMF. Controlling world population is not a function of any international organization, let alone the WTO.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason for the growth of international trade in the 15th century?
choices: Because of the discovery of new lands
Because of the use of barter
Because of the decline in population
Because of the increase in agriculture
questions.solution: The growth of international trade in the 15th century was due to the discovery of new lands, which opened up new routes and markets for exchange. Barter was a common method of trade long before the 15th century and did not specifically drive its growth. A decline in population would likely reduce trade, not increase it. An increase in agriculture could support trade but was not a direct cause of the expansion of international trade during this period.

questions.stem: Which of the following best represents the purpose of trade agreements like the General Agreement for Tariffs and Trade (GATT)?
choices: To restrict international trade and promote local markets
To encourage trade between countries with geographical proximity and similar or complementary trading items
To replace global organizations and regulate all international trade activities globally
To enforce trade tariffs between member nations and prevent free trade agreements
questions.solution: The purpose of trade agreements like GATT is to encourage trade between countries with geographical proximity and similar or complementary trading items. These agreements aim to reduce trade barriers and foster economic cooperation. The other options are incorrect because they suggest restrictions, global replacement of organizations, or enforcement of tariffs, which do not align with the goal of promoting trade.
